artists.biography:
The Lemonheads are an American alternative rock band first formed in 1986 by Evan Dando, Ben Deily and Jesse Peretz. Dando has remained the band's only constant member.

Since its formation, recording and touring lineups of the band have included co-founders Deily and Peretz, John Strohm (Blake Babies), Doug Trachten, Corey Loog Brennan, Byron Hoagland (Folks On Fire), Ben Daughtrey (Squirrel Bait), Juliana Hatfield (Blake Babies), Nic Dalton (Godstar, Sneeze, The Plunderers), Dave Ryan, Patrick "Murph" Murphy (Dinosaur Jr), Bill Gibson (Eastern Dark), Mark 'Budola' Newman, Kenny Lyon, Vess Ruhtenberg, Devon Ashley, Karl Alvarez and Bill Stevenson (Descendents), P. David Hazel and various others.

After their initial punk-influenced releases and tours as an independent/"college rock" band in the late '80s, the Lemonheads' popularity with a mass audience grew in 1992 with the major label album It's a Shame about Ray, which was produced, engineered, and mixed by The Robb Brothers (Bruce Robb, Dee, and Joe). This was followed by a cover of Simon and Garfunkel's "Mrs. Robinson", which eventually became one of the band's most successful singles. The Lemonheads were active until 1997 before going on hiatus, but reformed with a new lineup in 2005 and released The Lemonheads the following year. The band released its latest album, Varshons, in June 2009.

perplexity.description:
The Lemonheads - Lick (1989) represents the band's debut full-length album and marked a pivotal moment in their early career. Released on the independent Taang! label, Lick showcases the group's formative sound, oscillating between punk-pop energy and folky-pop sensibilities. The album's eclectic composition draws from multiple recording sessions, combining six newly recorded tracks with material from various earlier sources, creating an unconventional but cohesive debut statement.

As the final album released before The Lemonheads signed to major label Atlantic Records, Lick captures the band at a transitional juncture in their development. The record established foundational elements of their aesthetic while documenting the creative output of a young group still defining their artistic direction. The album's hybrid approach—blending punk-influenced arrangements with melodic, acoustic-driven compositions—would become characteristic of the band's broader catalog.

Lick stands as a significant artifact of late-1980s independent rock, documenting The Lemonheads' emergence from the Boston underground scene before their subsequent mainstream breakthrough. The album's raw production values and stylistic diversity reflect the band's experimental approach during their formative years, making it an essential reference point for understanding their evolution as songwriters and performers.
